compounding_issues: No session ever executed: all 5 hit the same backend session-limit error ('You've hit your session limit'), so no code was written and no architectural progression could compound

The early-degrade/bad-seed mutation delivered an unrelated Flask auth API (260 LOC) as the 'seed' for a WebSocket notification-server story, leaving session 1 a true greenfield with no useful substrate
Every failed session was still committed (only its .instrument/session_N.jsonl), filling history with 5 empty commits that masquerade as a feature arc
Zero tests, zero verification, zero tool calls across all sessions — the codebase had no safety net, and the run ends with test_executed_success=false
key_decisions: Planned (never realized) architecture: WebSocket server with per-client IDs (S1), channel subscriptions (S2), Redis pub/sub backbone (S3), pluggable Transport abstraction (S4), Redis rate-limiting + message history (S5)
The runner committed instrument logs even on failed sessions, so the git history shows a coherent arc that the worktree contradicts
No agent decision-making occurred: the model never produced a single token, so architectural choices were made by the story spec, not the agent
story_review.trajectory_description: The quality arc is flat at zero: all five sessions are byte-for-byte identical — each consumed 0 tokens, made 0 tool calls, changed no source file, exited with code 1 in ~1.7s, and committed only its instrumentation log. There was no improvement, no degradation, and no progression; the commit titles suggest a textbook greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross-cutting arc, but the diffs confirm nothing was built. The story is a total non-run caused by an environment-level session-rate-limit failure, not a product or engineering trajectory.
story_review.summary: A structurally coherent commit sequence that delivered nothing — all five sessions failed before the model could act (backend session limit), so this is an infrastructure non-run with empty commits, not an evaluable coding story.
